condition: compulsive mirror checking focused on the nose for 4 hours daily over 6 months keeping a young adult homebound from work
level_rationale: Six months of getting stuck in compulsive mirror-checking routines focused on the nose for 4 hours every day that keeps a 23-year-old adult home from work indicates severe functionally disabling body dysmorphic disorder requiring psychiatrist evaluation for high-dose serotonergic pharmacotherapy and specialized cognitive behavioral therapy, whereas glancing at the nose in the mirror for 2 minutes each morning before heading to work reflects ordinary daily grooming requiring no medical care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg, Brennan 2023) + unsourced vanity causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact mirror-checking severity de-escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (age 23, 6-month daily mirror focus on the nose, and 4-hour daily checking routines keeping the speaker home from work) obeying Hard Limit 7 without naming body dysmorphic disorder, with a 2-word span difference (23 vs 25 words) and zero stated negatives. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, overriding plan.json's banned 40 C neuroleptic-rigidity swap to make the same mirror-checking behavior milder (2 minutes each morning before heading to work) shifts care cleanly from psychiatrist treatment (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
